measurement: Registered kill files for usage_lineage (validation/v2/mutation.py:806): tests/v2/test_v21_kills3_A08.py, tests/v2/test_v21_kills3_T08a.py, tests/v2/test_v21_kills3_T08b.py. Baseline (unmutated) GREEN: 20 tests OK. Each of the 13 mutants: 20 tests OK (PASS) -> SURVIVED-by-measurement confirmed for all 13; none REFUTED-by-measurement. Run env: PATH stripped of the two dirs holding an executable opencode, HOME/TMPDIR under the run tree, PYTHONPATH=run-tree-root, nice -n 19 /opt/homebrew/bin/python3 -P -B -m unittest. Why they survive: all three files exercise only the normal (readable) path and pass `own` with no 'sessions' key, so they never enter the except branch (lineage.py:801-806) and own_blind (L819) is always `any(... for x in [])` == False.

entries.group: UL-BLIND-REDUNDANT: `blind` is redundant with the per-run `unaccounted` check for the only trigger that can set it.
entries.grounds: `blind` is written True only in the except branch (lineage.py:802) and read only at L820 (`exact = not blind and not any(a['unaccounted'] ...) and ...`). The except branch (L801) is entered only when `events_of(d)` (L798) or `usage.usage(d, ...)` (L799) raises. events_of NEVER raises: it wraps read_text+reconstruct in try/except and returns None on failure (lineage.py:168-171), so `got[0] if got else []` is [] and the L799 comprehension iterates only well-formed reconstructed Event objects. So the sole trigger is usage.usage raising, which happens only when a session file's read_bytes() fails inside session_tokens->client.events (usage.py:52, client.py:44). The SAME run's account_of reads the identical file through the identical client.events (Budget.spend->read_session->events, client.py:97-98,57) and catches the failure into that run's unaccounted/unread (lineage.py:509-515); client.py:36 and usage.py:51 state this is deliberately the one shared reading. account['runs'][i] IS that account_of(path) dict (lineage.py:727). Therefore whenever `blind` is set for a run, that run's acct['unaccounted'] is non-empty, so any(a['unaccounted'] for a in account['runs']) is True and `exact` is False regardless of `blind`. `blind` can never change any output. Measurement: kill files PASS on mutant and baseline.
consumers_checked: aisef2/app/usage.py:52 session_tokens, aisef2/app/client.py:44 events, client.py:97-98,57 Budget.spend/read_session (the single shared stream reader for both usage.usage and account_of)
exceptions_checked: a run reaching the except branch with EMPTY unaccounted: impossible -- the trigger is a read_bytes failure that account_of reads identically and records in that run's unaccounted (lineage.py:509-515)
events_of raising instead of returning None: it catches every exception and returns None (lineage.py:168-171)
the L799 comprehension raising on a reconstructed event: reconstruct yields Event objects with .seq/.type/.data and dict-able data

entries.group: UL-OWNBLIND: L819 own_blind drives tokens_status from THIS run's own sessions; the registered kill files never pass `own` with a 'sessions' list, so the whole clause is uncovered.
entries.grounds: own_blind (L819) is on the always-evaluated normal path and reads this run's own sessions via own.get('sessions'); in production own = rec['usage'] = usage.usage output, which always carries 'sessions' with per-session 'steps'/'steps_without_tokens' (usage.py:84,113; run.py:671-672). own_blind -> exact (L820) -> tokens_status (L823), an operator-visible, documented field (docstring L790-791; ADR-V2.1:170; docs/v2.1/USAGE-2.1.md:221). The mutation turns `not x.get('steps')` into `+x.get('steps')`: a fully-tokened own session (steps>0, steps_without_tokens=0) gives `0 or +steps` == steps (truthy) -> own_blind True -> tokens_status wrongly 'lower bound' for a fully-known lineage (and a no-steps session, steps==0, flips the other way: `0 or +0` == 0 -> own_blind False -> wrongly 'known'). The three registered kill files pass `own` with no 'sessions' (A08 own={tokens,cost}; T08a own={tokens:{},cost}; T08b OWN has no sessions) so own_blind is any(...) over [] == False and the mutant is invisible. Even the non-registered intent test test_v21_x_lineage_proof.py:245 uses steps_without_tokens=1 (truthy), which short-circuits BEFORE the mutated clause. Measurement: kill files PASS on mutant.
consumers_checked: aisef2/app/run.py:671-672 (own = usage.usage output, always has 'sessions' with steps/steps_without_tokens)
exceptions_checked: own with no sessions: own_blind over [] -> False in both -> exactly the registered tests' case, hence the miss
a session with steps_without_tokens>0: the `or` short-circuits truthy in both -> the mutated `not steps` clause is never the decider
entries.refutation: input: a clean lineage (every predecessor recorded and fully accounted, none blind, so not any(unaccounted) and all recorded) with own = {'tokens':{...}, 'cost':{'value':x,'status':'known'}, 'sessions':[{'session':'S1.developer.1.jsonl','steps':1,'steps_without_tokens':0}]}. reader: usage_lineage's exact/tokens_status (lineage.py:820-823), read by the operator from RUN.json lineage_usage.tokens_status. sketch: call lineage.usage_lineage(...); assert result['tokens_status'] == 'known'. Original passes; mutant 71 computes own_blind=True -> 'lower bound'. (A second case with an own session steps=0 additionally pins 71.) Add to tests/v2/test_v21_kills3_T08b.py (also kills index 109).

entries.group: UL-OWNBLIND: L819 own_blind drives tokens_status from THIS run's own sessions; the registered kill files never pass `own` with a 'sessions' list, so the whole clause is uncovered.
entries.grounds: In own_blind (L819), `not x.get('steps')` becomes `not x.get('')`. x.get('') is None for every session row, so `not None` == True, making own_blind = any(x.get('steps_without_tokens') or True for x in own.get('sessions') or []) == True whenever this run has >=1 own session. In production own = usage.usage output, which yields >=1 session row whenever the run ran any session (usage.py:84,113), so tokens_status is forced to 'lower bound' even for a fully-known lineage. Same consumer chain and operator/doc contract as index 71. The registered kill files pass `own` with no 'sessions' -> own_blind over [] -> False -> invisible; the non-registered :245 uses steps_without_tokens=1 (truthy short-circuit) -> also invisible. Measurement: kill files PASS on mutant.

entries.group: UL-EXCEPT-STATUS-STRING: cosmetic edits to the parenthetical of the blind row's cost.status; the load-bearing tags 'unknown:' and 'its evidence cannot be read' survive and no reader parses the rest.
entries.grounds: Swaps `getattr(e, 'strerror', None) or e` -> `e or getattr(e, 'strerror', None)`. The caught exception e is always truthy, so `e or ...` always yields e, and the status shows str(e) instead of e.strerror. For the reachable trigger (an OSError from read_bytes, which has a truthy .strerror) this changes 'Permission denied' -> '[Errno 13] Permission denied: \'/path/S1.jsonl\'' (str(e)) -- more verbose, still conveying the cause, truncated to [:300] (L805); the path is the operator's own run path in the operator's own RUN.json (no cross-trust boundary). For an exception with no truthy strerror the two are identical (client.events decodes with errors='replace', so no UnicodeDecodeError arises). The 'unknown:'/'cannot be read' tags are unchanged. No consumer parses the message. Observable, but nothing depends on strerror-vs-str(e). Measurement: kill files PASS (except branch never built).
